Android Auto Users Claim Gemini Is Just Playing a Random Song on Amazon Music
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
Gemini was supposed to provide a significantly upgraded experience on Android Auto, but now that Google Assistant is dead , more and more users discover that this isn’t happening. The latest glitch that seems to be plaguing Android Auto users after the forced transition to Gemini concerns the ability to play a song when requested with a voice command.
More specifically, users discovered that listening to music on Amazon Music is suddenly more difficult after Gemini became the one and only AI-powered assistant on Android Auto.
This is because Gemini seems to ignore users’ voice commands, playing a random song whenever it’s requested to play a specific track. In plain English, Gemini plays whatever song it wants, no matter what tune it’s requested to load.
This only happens in Amazon Music, and users claim that the glitch appeared once Google Assistant was retired.
“Gemini does not work with Amazon Music. I initially went back to using Google Assistant with Android Auto, which played perfectly with Amazon Music,” someone says in a post published in early October on Google’s forums .
“However, Gemini has now been forced upon us. I understand (from asking Gemini!) that Google needs to create an app extension for Amazon Music to resolve this (and that Google Assistant worked differently and didn't require one), but apparently there is no timescale for when / if this might happen.”
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Several others joined the conversation, and as it turns out, this is what more users are experiencing on Android Auto after the transition from Google Assistant to Gemini. Everybody is reporting the same glitch, with Gemini just playing a random song instead of the track it’s requested to load in Amazon Music.
Oddly, not everybody is affected.
I just tried asking Gemini to play Metallica - Nothing Else Matters on Amazon Music, and the AI assistant followed the instructions correctly. Random songs don’t seem to be played in my car, so it’s clear that not everybody is affected. I use Android Auto 18.0 with a Google Pixel 10 Pro XL.
Interestingly, someone with the same phone says they do see the bug.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution “Using [the app] on my Android Auto device voice control to play a specific song, the song is first confirmed by Gemini, but then a casual song is played. I have an Amazon Music Unlimited subscription. I have a Pixel 10. All devices and Apps are up to date,” one user explains.
While Gemini failing to run a simple task isn’t necessarily surprising, especially considering the bugs the new AI-powered assistant has struggled with lately, users complain that Google Assistant worked correctly before it was discontinued.
Several users explained on the forums that this is precisely the reason why they went back from Gemini to Google Assistant when this option was still available. They downgraded because Gemini couldn’t play Amazon Music songs correctly, and going back to Google Assistant temporarily was seen by everybody as a way to continue to use the music streaming service until Google comes up with a patch.
Google doesn’t appear to have addressed the glitch, and now that going back to Google Assistant is no longer an option, users are being forced to look for other solutions.
“I am also suffering from the same issue. When Gemini was initially pushed on my device around 5 months ago I switched back to assistant and provided this reason (lack of voice control for Amazon music when using Android Auto) as the reason. Now Gemini has been forced up on us, and Amazon Music still doesn't work. Very poor from Google,” someone explains.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The problem is that no workaround has been found for this glitch. The typical Android Auto fixes don’t seem to correct the error, as clearing the cache, reinstalling and updating Android Auto, and everything else that might resolve an Android Auto issue don’t make a difference. This means that a patch from Google is the only way to continue to use Amazon Music with Gemini, so without it, users are forced to just avoid voice commands entirely.
A Google Community Specialist replied on October 7 and revealed that additional information about the glitch is necessary. Users who reported the problem were contacted by email to provide more data, so right now, it’s unclear if the investigation has made any progress.
Meanwhile, keeping automatic app updates enabled is highly recommended for users battling this error. Once Google releases a fix, you should get it as an automatic update, though it’s unclear when this is supposed to happen. Android Auto 18.0 has just started rolling out, but it doesn’t seem to include a fix - let me know in the comments box below if this new version corrected the Gemini and Amazon Music problem for you.
Google hasn’t offered additional data, so share your experience with Gemini and Amazon Music in the comments box below if you want to help the search giant come up with a fix faster.
